title: reveal_secret / rotate_secret run unlimited password_verify with no throttle or lockout
description: The reveal-after-owner-password gate (Actions.php:255-267) and rotate handler (Actions.php:268-280) verify the submitter's password with password_verify on every POST but apply no attempt counter, delay, or lockout. The login flow enforces a per-session limit of 8 bad attempts per 900s plus a 250ms sleep (index.php:23-40), but that bad_logins state is session-keyed and never consulted by the reveal/rotate handlers. Both handlers sit behind require_login() + require_csrf() and role==owner/admin + !active_support(), so the brute-force precondition is an already-authenticated owner/admin session (e.g. obtained via XSS/CSRF token leak or an unattended logged-in device). Static source fully establishes the missing control; real-world exploitation additionally requires the authenticated-session precondition, so exploitability is validated rather than asserted.
